## Diagnosis

The error-recovery path in `parse_binding` (parser.py:169-176) calls `reader.read_regex(_rest_of_line)`, where `_rest_of_line = r"[^
]*(?:|
|
)?"`. The alternation tries `` before `
`, so on a CRLF it consumes only the ``, leaving the `
` for the next binding. The next `parse_binding` then reads `
` as leading whitespace and the valid line's `original.string` becomes `"
GOOD=ok
"` with `line=2` (line count still advances correctly via `advance`), and the invalid binding's `original.string` ends with a bare ``.

## Change plan

In `src/dotenv/parser.py`, reorder the alternation in `_rest_of_line` to `r"[^
]*(?:
||
)?"` so CRLF is matched as one unit. This makes the invalid binding's `original.string` include the full `
`, and the following valid binding start cleanly at line 2 with `original.string == "GOOD=ok
"`. LF and lone-CR behavior are unchanged (each still matches its single terminator), and repeated invalid lines each consume their own complete newline. No other files need edits; existing tests in `tests/test_parser.py` should continue to pass.

Result: invalid binding's original.string ends with bare `\\r`, and the valid binding's original.string becomes `\"\\nGOOD=ok\\n\"` instead of `\"GOOD=ok\\n\"`.\n\nPlan: Reorder the alternation to `r\"[^\\r\\n]*(?:\\r\\n|\\r|\\n)?\"` so CRLF is consumed as one newline. LF and lone-CR behavior stay identical, and repeated invalid lines each consume their own terminator. Single-line change in src/dotenv/parser.py; no other files."}
